longForm.heroHook: 8 load cells. 100g to 100kg. 500 Hz data capture. One instrument, two test types.
longForm.heroLead: Most texture analyzers force a choice: sensitive enough for soft samples, or strong enough for firm ones. Not both. CTX Texture Analyzer removes that trade-off with 8 interchangeable load cells spanning 100g to 100kg — soft cosmetic gels and firm baked goods on the same instrument. Both compression and tension testing run on one platform. No swapping to a second instrument for the other test type. Speed matters when texture attributes happen fast — a fracture, a rupture, the exact moment a product breaks. CTX captures data at 500 Hz, fast enough to catch that peak instead of averaging past it. Reach: boom travel up to 280mm, for larger or more complex samples. Flexibility: 3 adjustable base tables, for varied sample shapes and sizes. Compliance: optional Texture Pro Software brings 21 CFR Part 11 compliance for regulated industries.

sections.tabSummary: What 8 load cells and 3 base tables cover, combined
body: CTX Texture Analyzer load cell range: soft samples, firm samples, one instrument.
A texture measurement is only as good as the load cell measuring it. Too sensitive, and a firm product saturates the reading instantly. Not sensitive enough, and a soft gel barely registers.

CTX solves this with 8 interchangeable load cells spanning 100g to 100kg. No compromise built into a single fixed sensor — the same instrument tests a soft cosmetic and a firm food product, accurately, both.

3 adjustable base tables extend that same flexibility to the sample itself — different shapes, different sizes, no forcing everything onto one fixed platform. Combine that with 280mm of boom travel, and larger or more complex samples that a shorter-reach tester simply couldn't handle become testable.

cards.description: The exact peak force at break

cards.title: A product ruptures under pressure
cards.description: The precise moment, not an approximation

paragraphs: Some texture events happen fast. A fracture. A rupture. The instant a firm product's surface breaks. If the data acquisition rate is too slow, that exact peak gets lost — averaged away instead of captured.

CTX runs at 500 Hz, specifically to catch those precise moments of change. That matters most on brittle or fracturing materials, where the peak force at the point of break is often the actual measurement — not an average across the whole test.
